criteria.criterion: Both `cat-file blob` reads in `_read_blob_bytes` receive `_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS`; a new unit test recording the timeout each `_git` call receives fails before the change and passes after.
`_object_type` receives `_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS` from every caller, asserted by the same test on the read path and during a `set_gate` CAS advance over a legacy blob tip.
`update-ref` calls in `_ref_lock.py` still receive `_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS`, asserted by the same test.

A new test builds a real `--filter=blob:none` clone of a local bare repo holding a `refs/reconciler/lock` commit and shows `read()` returns the released lock state, with the payload blob absent locally before the read.

`docs/adr/0121-reconciler-architecture-consolidated-record.md` §10 states that object reads (`cat-file`) use the 30 s remote budget because a partial clone may fetch them lazily; `git diff origin/main -- docs/adr/0031-reconciler-ref-lock.md` is empty.
